name: Reformed Dogmatika Confessions Library
author: reformeddogmatika

sections.description:
Reformed Dogmatika Confessions Library makes the historic Reformed confessions easy to reference. Cite “WCF 11.1” or “Heidelberg Catechism Q&A 1” in any post, and readers get a hover preview and click-to-open full passage. Every reference also has a local reading page that works without JavaScript. Optional external source-edition links are off by default.

Seventeen documents, 1,358 referenced items included locally:

  • The Three Forms of Unity: Belgic Confession, Heidelberg Catechism, Canons of Dort
  • The Westminster Standards: Confession of Faith, Shorter Catechism, Larger Catechism
  • Early Reformed confessions: First and Second Helvetic, Geneva Catechism, Consensus Tigurinus, French Confession, Zwingli’s Sixty-Seven Articles, Ten Theses of Bern
  • The ecumenical creeds: Apostles’, Nicene, Athanasian, and the Chalcedonian Formula

Features

  • Automatic citation linking. Plain-text citations in your published content (“WCF 3.1”, “Westminster Confession of Faith (3.1)”, “Heidelberg Catechism Q&A 60”, “Canons of Dort, First Head, Article 7”) become popup links automatically. No content edits required; disable any time.
  • Shortcodes. [rdcl_wsc 1], [rdcl_wcf 11.1], [rdcl_hc 60], [rdcl_cd 2.3], [rdcl_ac], and more. Modes: popup (default), inline card, citation-only. Custom link text via text=””.
  • Hover popups and modals. Keyboard and touch controls, no jQuery, vanilla JavaScript. Without JavaScript, citation links open the full passage locally.
  • Cross-confessional search. Drop [rdcl_confession_search] on a page for a ranked, highlighted search across all 1,358 items.
  • Local reading. Open complete passages from search results, follow previous/next passages, and consult translation and licensing notes. Native form submission keeps search usable without JavaScript or REST access.
  • Read-only REST API. Endpoints for documents, single items, and search, for study tools and integrations.
  • Settings page. Toggles for auto-linking, popups, external source links, and the REST API under Settings > Reformed Dogmatika Confessions Library.

Texts are packaged locally by Reformed Dogmatika. Translation attribution and reuse notices are recorded in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt. Source links are optional and off by default. A site owner may opt in under Settings > Reformed Dogmatika Confessions Library.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin through Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin, or install from the directory.
  2. Activate it.
  3. That’s it. Citations in your content begin linking automatically. Optionally add [rdcl_confession_search] to a page and review Settings > Reformed Dogmatika Confessions Library.
sections.faq:
Which translations/editions are used?

The collection includes historical English editions and Peter Chapman’s First Helvetic Confession translation, licensed under CC BY 4.0. Consensus Tigurinus uses Henry Beveridge’s 1849 translation. See THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt and the local Text sources and licenses page for edition distinctions, attribution, packaging changes, and documented textual corrections. The collection is not represented as a diplomatic transcription of every printed source.

Does it phone home or load anything external?

All texts ship inside the plugin as JSON. The plugin makes no background requests to external services and performs no tracking. Search requests stay on your own site. A visitor who follows an optional external source link leaves your site and contacts that publisher or archive normally.

Are external links required?

No. Citations and popup footers open local reading pages. Only after a site owner opts in under Settings > Reformed Dogmatika Confessions Library > Source links do inline cards, search results, and reading pages include links to external source editions. The publishers and archives are identified in the bundled notices. These are ordinary hyperlinks, not embedded third-party services.

Can I disable the automatic linking?

Yes, in Settings, or per-site with the rclib_autolink_enabled filter.

Can this run alongside the private RD Confessions Library plugin?

The public plugin has separate classes, settings, asset handles, and interface selectors. Its shortcodes use the rdcl_ prefix. When the private RD plugin is also active, it retains ownership of automatic citation linking; the public plugin’s explicit shortcodes, search, and local reading pages remain available. This is not an automatic migration of existing private-plugin settings or shortcode content.

Are abbreviations like WCF and WSC supported?

Yes: WCF, WSC, WLC, HC, BC, CD, and SHC (uppercase), plus full document names, with or without parentheses.
sections.changelog:
1.0.3

  • Rename the plugin and directory slug to identify Reformed Dogmatika as the publisher. Functionality is unchanged from 1.0.2.

1.0.2

  • Add local full-passage reading and native search fallbacks.
  • Fix Plain permalink search, discarded search tokens, stale results, and multiple search widgets.
  • Honor popup settings on existing links and isolate public-plugin internals.
  • Replace Consensus Tigurinus with Beveridge’s 1849 text and record source-verified corrections.
  • Add edition provenance, Chapman CC BY 4.0 attribution, and bundled license text.

1.0.1

  • Prefix all public identifiers and shortcodes to prevent conflicts.
  • Make external source links opt-in and off by default.
  • Confirm compatibility through WordPress 7.1.

1.0.0

  • Initial public release: 17 documents, 1,358 items, auto-linking, shortcodes, popups, modals, search, REST API, settings.
